Cyclone Arnab: Schools and Colleges Closed in Parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal

Regional Closures Announced Amid Weather Warnings

Educational institutions in several districts of Tamil Nadu, along with the union territory regions of Puducherry and Karaikal, have declared holidays due to heavy rainfall and anticipated cyclone-related weather conditions. The precautionary closures affect schools in specific districts including Dindigul, Coimbatore, The Nilgiris, and Theni, while neighboring regions like Chengalpattu continue to operate as usual.

The administrative decisions follow persistent downpours, waterlogging in low-lying areas, and localized disruptions to road transport. Authorities implemented the shutdowns to ensure the safety of students and staff traveling to and from campuses as a developing weather system tracked toward the Andhra Pradesh coast.

District-Wise Status and Scope of Disruptions

School holiday announcements vary significantly by locality, emphasizing that closures are not statewide:

  • Dindigul & Coimbatore: Schools are closed due to heavy rainfall and prevailing weather conditions.
  • The Nilgiris: Closures specifically cover educational institutions in Udhagamandalam, Coonoor, Kotagiri, and Kundah taluks.
  • Theni: Restrictions apply to schools located in the Periyakulam taluk.
  • Chengalpattu: Schools and colleges remain open, functioning according to normal schedules.
  • Chennai: Residents are advised to monitor official district communications for any updates regarding operational changes.

In Puducherry and Karaikal, the administration extended closures to encompass all government, government-aided, and private colleges alongside schools, responding to travel safety concerns caused by standing water on roadways.

Official Guidance and What Remains Uncertain

While safety protocols have forced immediate campus closures, several operational questions depend on individual institutional policies:

  • Online Classes: Educational institutions may offer digital lessons or homework depending on their capabilities, but families must confirm instructions directly with their respective schools rather than assuming virtual attendance is mandatory.
  • Examinations: Routine closures do not automatically postpone official board or university tests. Students with scheduled public examinations must consult specific notifications from relevant examination boards.
  • Future Outlook: The trajectory and intensity of the weather system remain subject to change. District administrations continue to monitor meteorological forecasts and may issue further orders if conditions evolve.
